headlines.title: China’s backflipping robots leap to blockbuster stock market debut in latest sign of AI boom
headlines.description: Unitree’s shares closed up 460% on Wednesday, a significant marker as Beijing competes with Washington for global tech dominance.

headlines.title: Gov. Josh Shapiro takes a hard line against ‘predatory’ data center developers in Pennsylvania
headlines.description: Shapiro, a potential Democratic 2028 contender, earlier welcomed data center developments. His new executive order takes a starkly different tone toward the industry.

headlines.title: Trump says he will meet with Kim Jong Un this year
headlines.description: President Trump told reporters that he expects to meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un this year. NBC News' Courtney Kube reports on the comments shortly after the president announced military exercises with South Korea would be scaled back.

headlines.title: Unitree unveils ‘Superman’ humanoid robot
headlines.description: Chinese robotics company Unitree unveiled a new humanoid robot dubbed “Superman” which it says is “breaking the limits of humanity.” According to the company, the robot can perform a vertical jump of over 6 feet and can reach a top speed of more than 40 feet per second.

headlines.title: Calif. AG Rob Bonta hopes Meta trial would improve child safety on social media platforms
headlines.description: California Attorney General Rob Bonta speaks with NBC News’ Gadi Schwartz about the trial against Meta, which alleges that Facebook and Instagram were intentionally designed in ways that harm young users’ mental health, and discusses the changes he is seeking for these platforms.

headlines.title: Radio show with an A.I. host expands to new markets
headlines.description: A new kind of radio show is finding a growing audience. It features a unique format, one of its two hosts is human, and the other is A.I. The show is now expanding to new markets. NBC Los Angeles Reporter Amber Frias caught up with the human host.

headlines.title: States take on Meta in court over child addiction claims
headlines.description: State attorneys general are in court arguing that Meta knowingly created features on its social media platforms that keep children addicted. NBC News' Allie Canal reports on the court case and impact it could have on the tech company.

headlines.title: How AI Has Become a Fixture in Classrooms and Homes
headlines.description: Students are heading back to school equipped with books, backpacks, and increasingly, artificial intelligence. Seven in 10 teens now say they are using AI tools for schoolwork, according to a new survey from Common Sense Media. Despite the technology’s prevalence, however, students say they’re not getting a lot of guidance from teachers around how and when to use it. NBC’s Emilie Ikeda reports for TODAY.

headlines.title: Meta Faces New Youth Social Media Addiction Suit After $1B Loss
headlines.description: After losing a nearly $1 billion legal battle in New Mexico for knowingly harming the mental health of children, Meta is headed back to court. This time it will face state attorneys general from four states accusing the social media giant behind Facebook and Instagram of knowingly creating an algorithm that is addictive, especially for teenage users. NBC’s Laura Jarrett shares a preview of the case for TODAY.

headlines.title: Dating apps bet big on A.I. to fight 'swipe fatigue' and reshape the search for love
headlines.description: Major dating apps like Grindr are opting for more A.I. in order to make better matches, as studies show Americans are connecting less overall. NBC News' Allie Canal reports on the tech increasingly at the heart of matchmaking on the apps right now.

headlines.title: Thousands of Americans roll the dice on travel with viral 'Mystery Vacation' trend
headlines.description: Viral Groupon "Mystery Vacations" promise trips for as little as $200, but the catch, you have no idea where you're going until after you've paid. NBC News’ Ryan Chandler spoke to some buyers who scored their dream trips and others who were not so lucky.

headlines.title: Flock CEO Addresses Backlash Over Surveillance Cameras
headlines.description: More than 120,000 Flock cameras are monitoring roads across 7,000 cities nationwide but there’s growing public outrage over privacy concerns and multiple reports of police misuse. In response to the criticism, the surveillance company is unveiling what it calls a major overhaul to its protocols. NBC’s Brian Cheung reports for TODAY and speaks to Flock founder and CEO Garrett Langley about the backlash.
